The one call I did not simply ratify

You said "decide for me" on the two findings. On N1 · the cap chip I overrode my own sketch. Sheet 04 had proposed keeping the chip on the bare cap while syncing only its over/under state — which manages the contradiction rather than removing it, and still shows a user 1.600/1.500 while calling it fine.

Decided instead: when pooling is active, both surfaces use the pooled budget. The chip reads 268/1.760 km. One denominator, one verdict, no reconciliation logic to get wrong. The bare cap survives only where it is defined — the gauge's own line, 1.500 cap + 260 carried over from June. Sheet 04 is updated.

01 · #13 · The missed-fill toggle

The flag shaped economy intervals and appeared on record pages, but no user could ever set it. Without this control it was import-only.
THE FUEL SHEET · OFF (DEFAULT)
Discard Fill-up Save
35,75 € 26,10 1,370
ODOMETER
91.240 km
Full tank Repsol ▾
A fill was missed before this one
ON · THE CONSEQUENCE IS STATED IMMEDIATELY
Discard Fill-up Save
35,75 € 26,10 1,370
ODOMETER
91.240 km
Full tank Repsol ▾
A fill was missed before this one
This fill won't measure economy. Your next full tank starts a fresh interval.

Worded as a fact, not a confession

A fill was missed before this one — passive, no "you", no "forgot". Compare the version this replaces: "I forgot to log a fill" makes the ledger a place you can fail. The app does not scold, and this is the single most likely place for scolding to creep in.

A switch, not a chip — because it is not an option

The chip row above it holds choices (full tank, station, date). This is an assertion about data quality, and it costs the user a computed number — so it sits below a rule, in the switch idiom, and says what it costs the moment it is on.

It only renders when it can be true

Hidden on a car's first fill (nothing precedes it) and hidden when fullTank is off (a partial does not close an interval, so the flag would change nothing). A control that cannot affect anything is worse than a missing one.

02 · #5 and #16 · Two lines on the Cost lens

One caps the bar list; the other admits the page is built partly on disputed data. Both are ink, and neither raises alarm.

Arithmetic: 289,00 + 214,00 + 123,10 + 68,40 + 24,30 + 23,80 = 742,60 €. Six rows, five named kinds plus Other · 2 — still summing to the headline exactly, which is the whole point of capping with a row rather than a truncation.

#5 · Other is a row, never a truncation

Cutoff at five named kinds. The sixth row aggregates the rest and carries its count — Other · 2, so the user knows how much is folded, not merely that something is.

Its bar is hairline grey, not a domain hue: it is mixed-kind money, and the four hues each mean one kind. Sorting it last regardless of size is deliberate — it is a container, not a category, so it must not compete for the eye with a real one.

#16 · The disputed-data line

One quiet ink sentence under the headline, with a link to the queue. Not attention, not a badge on the bars, not a suppressed chart.

The reasoning: the figures are still the best available, so the line is a receipt rather than a warning. Colouring it attention would imply the page is wrong; hiding it would let a confident chart stand on data the user has not accepted. This is article 4 turned on Insights itself.

Where the line appears

On any lens whose page contains a flagged reading — Cost, Fuel and Distance alike, since a disputed odometer moves all three. Ownership is exempt: it has no period, so "in this period" would be meaningless. It disappears the moment the queue is empty.

Why March, not July

July's fixture has four kinds and a clean queue, so neither state could be shown on it honestly. Rather than bend the fixture, this frame pages back to a month that genuinely has six kinds and an open flag — 742,60 €, its own arithmetic, reconciled in its own right.

03 · #8 and #15 · The queued undo, and ownership across a swap

One is a data-loss bug with a copy fix; the other decides what "this car" means when the car has been replaced.
#8 · TWO DELETES INSIDE SIX SECONDS
BEFORE · THE FIRST UNDO IS LOST
Reading deleted. Undo
↓
Fill deleted. Undo
The reading is now permanent, silently. Its closure went with the toast.
AFTER · THE CLOSURES QUEUE
2 records deleted. Undo
One toast, one Undo, both restored. Each closure still lives its own 6 s.

This was a data-loss bug, not a copy problem

One-toast-at-a-time plus an in-memory closure meant the second delete silently made the first permanent. The user was offered an undo, did nothing wrong, and lost it.

The fix separates two things that were wrongly coupled: the toast is a view, the closure is state. Toasts still supersede one another visually; closures accumulate and each expires on its own timer. The collapsed copy — 2 records deleted. — is then just an honest label for a queue that already exists. It needs the app-level toast host the shell sheet calls for; per-screen toasts cannot hold a queue across a navigation.

#15 · OWNERSHIP · AFTER A SWAP · DARK
Since March 2025
Mapfre subscription · 2 cars
THE PLAN'S CARS

PoloMar 2025 – Sep 2025

THE RATES
Per month421,35 €

Over 17 months and 17.060 km, across both cars.

Not the §0.6 Golf — the fixture car has never been swapped. §0.6 cannot produce the state #15 asks about, so this is a hypothetical Polo → Golf swap on the same Mapfre plan, labelled as one. Note the two Mar 2025s are different facts: here it is the plan’s start, while the fixture’s Mar 2025 is the Golf’s tracking start — which is why the cost group reads since the plan began. The 17 charges are the plan’s, not the car’s.

The lens follows the plan, not the metal. Its title becomes Since March 2025 with a car count, and a THE PLAN'S CARS group replaces the ownership facts — because on a subscription there is no purchase price to state, and the question "what does this car cost me?" means the arrangement, not the vehicle currently parked outside.

Arithmetic: 4.913,00 + 1.842,60 + 310,50 + 96,80 = 7.162,90 €; ÷ 17 months = 421,35 €/mo; ÷ 17.060 km = 0,42 €/km. Plan charges are 17 × 289,00 = 4.913,00 €, which is only consistent because #1 made those charges real ledger rows.

The retired car is inkSoft, not dimmed — it is a closed chapter, not a degraded row. Same treatment as an archived car in the Garage list.
